observations.finding: Markedly reduced cell density / confluence in all 4 treated fields vs dense monolayer in DMSO control f_bd4169e2e78f. Large black background gaps. ~50-80 cells/field vs >300 in control. Cells more isolated, often larger spread area.

Tubulin (green in composite) visibly brighter and more heterogeneous. Thick bundles / high contrast texture, higher variance across cytoplasm vs diffuse dimmer green in DMSO. Read from composite only as no grayscale channel provided.
F-actin (red/orange rim) also brighter and more contrasty at cell periphery; increased STD / contrast vs DMSO where red is thin intercellular signal.

Nuclei (blue) increased size, irregular/lobulated shape, reduced solidity. Frequent bi-/multinucleated cells: many cytoplasmic units contain 2+ adjacent blue nuclei or single large multilobed nucleus. High incidence across all treated fields vs predominantly single round nuclei in DMSO.
Increased cell size with rounded / spread morphology; no obvious microtubule loss or actin collapse; no dense mitotic asters clearly resolvable in composite alone.

Fits Aurora kinase inhibition among provided list; Eg5 inhibitors is alternative mitotic target but Aurora more specifically linked to high multinucleation + solidity loss.

Secondary consideration: large tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast increase could also reflect stabilization/bundling, but decreased solidity + very high multinucleate fraction favors Aurora kinase inhibitors over pure stabilizer.

reflection.text:
Post-unblinding reflection - compound cycloheximide (recorded as cyclohexamide, PubChem CID 6197, ChEMBL CHEMBL123292, 80S Ribosome inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree; cycloheximide lookup same CID) - verdict correct: Protein synthesis. Scientist call (p=0.78) and protocol 1-NN majority vote both Protein synthesis; ground truth Protein synthesis.

What the evidence got right:

The quantitative dose series was decisive. We acquired 4 wells spanning 0.5 to 50 uM (e6 w_858491163f, e2 w_ae429219c6 1.5 uM, e3 w_6cce9eca32 15 uM, e7 w_8d51c42eb2 50 uM) after list_available_experiments showed 8 doses with budget for 4 wells. All 4 wells voted Protein synthesis by NSC (e4 2/2, e8 4/4) with similarity increasing with dose to 0.885 at 50 uM (protocol per-well 0.211 at 0.5 uM, 0.476 at 1.5 uM, 0.787 at 15 uM, 0.885 at 50 uM; summed similarity 2.359) and large margin over next k-neighbour classes Protein synthesis 5/10, Epithelial 4/10, Eg5 inhibitors 1/10.

The dose-response measurements were perfectly monotonic across the 4 wells and consistent with a strong, saturating phenotype: tub_mean rho=+1.00 (e11), frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+1.00 (e9), nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 (e10), cell_count rho=-1.00 (e12). Absolute effect sizes were extreme at high dose: tub_glcm_contrast z=+23.9 at 1.5 uM (e2) to z=+41.9 at 15 uM (e3) to z=+55.8 at 50 uM (e7), tub_mean z=+11.9 to +35.6 to +43.0, nuc_solidity z=-41.1 at 50 uM (e7), nuc_area z=-8.3 and cell_roundness z=+6.0 to +11.8 at low-mid doses (e6, e2). Direct well quantification also showed lower density vs DMSO (e5) matching cell_count rho=-1.00.

ChEMBL/lookup after review confirmed 80S Ribosome inhibitor mechanism for this structure, consistent with literature on 80S-targeting protein synthesis inhibitors PMID 32151059 and on inhibitors of protein synthesis on 80S ribosomes PMID 7201003. search_literature for 'cycloheximide 80S ribosome' returned 7 hits / 5 returned supporting this mechanism; the second search for morphology links returned 0 hits, so we had no independent literature to explain the tubulin/actin texture from that query and relied on atlas embedding.

What could have misled and why it did not:

The describe_phenotype read on 4 fields (e5) - composite-only visual comparison - suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors / Microtubule stabilizers due to lower density and multinucleation. That is plausible in isolation because frac_multinucleate_proxy increase and nuc_solidity loss (e9, e10) and tub_mean increase (e11) overlap with mitotic failure phenotypes (Aurora, Eg5). Hypothesis history retained those alternatives for this reason: Aurora 0.12 (supporting e5,e9,e10; contradicting e4,e8), Microtubule stabilizers 0.05 (supporting e5,e11), Eg5 inhibitors 0.05.

We down-weighted e5 correctly because: 1) it was based on 4 fields without single-cell quantification, versus 268-385 cells measured per well with quantitative texture/intensity; 2) NSC vote was unanimous 4/4 and monotonic in similarity, while k-neighbour tally already showed Epithelial/Eg5 as distant; 3) tubulin/actin glcm contrast changes were embedded by the reference atlas (Ljosa et al 2013 NSC) as Protein synthesis-like, not microtubule-stabilizer-like, at this dose range. Stating p=0.78 rather than 1.0 was calibrated given the conflicting visual read and single-replicate-per-dose design (0 wells left after 4 acquisitions, no replicate wells to estimate within-dose variance), but consistency across the dose series mitigated that limitation.

Acquisition choices:

Starting with mid (1.5 uM) and high (15 uM) anchors was efficient to detect onset vs strong effect, then adding threshold (0.5 uM) and saturation (50 uM) to test monotonicity. No errors flagged. All planned atlas/dose-response/phenotype analyses were exhausted, so no affordable additional step could have changed the call at submission, as review noted.

Missed / next step:

We did not have orthogonal translation inhibition data during the blind. The submitted rationale correctly proposed follow-up with puromycin incorporation / OPP click assay plus DNA content flow to distinguish translation inhibition from mitotic failure vs Aurora control at matched cytotoxicity.
